The model sees a coin flip tonight, with NYI at 3.13 expected goals and TOR at 3.11. NYI has controlled more of the play, taking 49% of the five-on-five expected goals to TOR's 44%. Both teams give up more chances than they create (NYI 2.75 for, 3.48 against per 60; TOR 2.99 for, 3.72 against), and both are leaning on results that outrun the chances. NYI is +4 in goals on -5.1 expected, with goaltending doing the lifting. TOR is +1 on -6.0 expected, helped by finishing and goaltending. On special teams, NYI's penalty kill allows 1.18 expected goals a game to TOR's 0.89, but NYI takes 5.0 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. TOR's power play generates 0.72 expected goals a game to NYI's 0.67.

The goalie matchup favors the visitors. Projected starter Ilya Sorokin is at .934 and +6.15 goals saved above expected through five games, after +22.3 over 55 games last season. Projected TOR starter Sergei Bobrovsky sits at .896 and +3.22 this year, after -13.5 over 52 games last season. Form is similar. NYI is 2-2-1 in its last five with 43% of the expected goals, TOR 2-1-2 with 45%. TOR won the first meeting 2-1 on Sep 30, a game it deserved 47% of the time.

Auston Matthews carries a 6-game point streak (6 G, 7 A) and a 39% chance to score, while William Nylander is at 40% to score and 71% for a point. For NYI, Bo Horvat has the highest scoring probability at 39%, and the model flags him as due to cool. Matias Maccelli has a 5-game point streak (2 G, 4 A) against his former team. Aatu Räty could also debut for TOR after joining from the Canucks.
